relevant_to: os; all flavors. Useful only when mysqld shares CPUs with NIC softirq, the benchmark client or other busy processes; no effect when the host is not CPU-saturated.

signals.metric: per-thread run-queue wait of mysqld threads (schedstat / eBPF runq latency)
signals.condition: a material share of connection-thread wall time is spent runnable-but-not-running while softirq/client/other processes use the same CPUs
signals.why: Confining mysqld away from the CPUs busy with interrupts/clients removes preemption and run-queue delay.

signals.metric: /proc/softirqs NET_RX/NET_TX per CPU and %soft per CPU (mpstat -P ALL)
signals.condition: softirq time is concentrated on a few CPUs that mysqld threads also run on
signals.why: Network softirq preempts mysqld threads on those CPUs and inflates query latency.

signals.metric: off-CPU category 'scheduler/run-queue' of connection threads
signals.condition: material share of foreground time
signals.why: Measures the time affinity could recover.

signals.metric: PSI cpu some avg10 (/proc/pressure/cpu or cgroup cpu.pressure)
signals.condition: high CPU pressure that coincides with low idle on a CPU subset
signals.why: Shows tasks waiting for CPU; affinity only helps if pressure is localized, it hurts if mysqld then has fewer CPUs than runnable threads.

impact_bound: At most the run-queue wait share of connection-thread time attributable to co-located softirq/clients; restricting CPUs also removes capacity, so the net gain is bounded by (run-queue wait recovered) - (CPU capacity lost). Typical: low to medium on small hosts with client on the same box or single-queue NICs; none on idle-CPU hosts.

experiment.change: pin mysqld to CPUs excluding those handling NIC IRQs (and the benchmark client), keep at least the CPUs mysqld actually uses at peak
experiment.predict: mysqld run-queue wait per trx falls; %soft on mysqld CPUs falls; mysqld CPU ms per trx flat or lower; throughput/latency improve
experiment.confirm_or_refute: Gain with lower run-queue wait confirms; if run-queue wait rises (fewer CPUs) or CPU on the pinned set hits 100%, refute and revert to all.
experiment.cost_or_risk: Loss of CPU capacity; NUMA side-effects if the set spans nodes inconsistently.

collected: partly - run-queue wait and PSI collected; add per-CPU softirq time (/proc/softirqs, mpstat %soft per CPU) and which CPUs run mysqld threads

relevant_to: os; bare metal or VMs that expose cpufreq (most clouds do not: /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq absent means no effect). Irrelevant when the CPU is mostly idle waiting for I/O.

signals.metric: /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor and scaling_cur_freq vs cpuinfo_max_freq during the run
signals.condition: governor is powersave/ondemand/schedutil and effective frequency during the run is materially below max
signals.why: Lower clock makes every CPU-bound microsecond longer.

signals.metric: perf stat cycles / task-clock (effective GHz) of mysqld, or turbostat Avg_MHz/Bzy_MHz
signals.condition: Bzy_MHz well below nominal/turbo while busy, or large variance between runs
signals.why: Direct measure of the frequency actually delivered to mysqld.

signals.metric: C-state residency (turbostat C6%) with short bursty load
signals.condition: latency-bound workload with frequent deep idle exits
signals.why: Wake-up from deep C-states and frequency ramp-up add latency to every request in light/bursty load.

impact_bound: Bounded by the CPU-on share of response time times (1 - cur_freq/max_freq); for latency-bound low-concurrency runs also the wake-up latency per request. Typical: medium (10-30%) on bare metal with powersave/ondemand; none on cloud VMs without cpufreq.

experiment.predict: effective MHz of mysqld rises; mysqld CPU ms per trx falls; latency falls in CPU-bound runs
experiment.confirm_or_refute: If MHz rises and CPU ms/trx falls proportionally, confirm; if MHz did not change (already max, or hypervisor controls clock) refute.
experiment.cost_or_risk: Higher power use/heat; can reduce turbo headroom on all-core loads slightly.

collected: no - add scaling_governor, scaling_cur_freq per CPU and perf cycles/task-clock (or turbostat) for mysqld

relevant_to: os; all flavors; only when a filesystem can be (re)created on the experiment device. Matters for I/O/commit-bound runs; none when data is fully cached and commits are cheap.

signals.metric: off-CPU redo flush (fsync) time and data page read/write wait of connection threads
signals.condition: a material share of foreground time is spent in fsync/fdatasync or file writes
signals.why: Filesystems differ in fsync cost (journal commit), allocation and O_DIRECT concurrency (ext4 vs xfs inode lock behavior).

signals.metric: fsync latency distribution (eBPF biolatency/fsync latency per file type) and jbd2/xfs log kernel thread CPU
signals.condition: fsync latency well above raw device write latency
signals.why: Excess over device latency is filesystem journaling overhead.

signals.metric: fsyncs per trx * mean fsync latency / trx latency
signals.condition: material share
signals.why: Upper bound of commit time a cheaper filesystem could save.

impact_bound: At most the share of foreground time in fsync and file I/O beyond raw device latency. Typical: low to medium (ext4 vs xfs usually within ~5-15% on NVMe; larger with high-concurrency O_DIRECT writes on ext4 or with many fsyncs).

experiment.change: recreate the datadir on xfs vs ext4 (same mount options, same device), reload data
experiment.predict: fsync latency and off-CPU redo flush time per trx fall; throughput rises
experiment.confirm_or_refute: Compare fsync latency and commit-wait time per trx; a throughput change without fsync/write-wait change is noise.
experiment.cost_or_risk: Requires reload/restart; durability semantics differ only with unsafe mount options.

collected: partly - off-CPU redo flush and fsyncs collected; add fsync/fdatasync latency histogram by file and journal thread CPU

relevant_to: os; all flavors; only when the drive has a volatile cache that is currently disabled. Drives with power-loss protection (most enterprise NVMe/SSD) report no volatile cache or ignore flush - no effect; cloud block devices usually no effect.

signals.metric: /sys/block/<dev>/queue/write_cache ('write back' vs 'write through'), hdparm -W, nvme get-feature -f 6
signals.condition: cache reported 'write through' on a drive that supports a volatile cache
signals.why: With cache off every write and flush waits for media; commits pay full media latency.

signals.metric: disk write await (w_await) per write I/O
signals.condition: write latency in the ms range on SSD/NVMe, or ~rotational latency on HDD
signals.why: Indicates writes going to media synchronously.

signals.metric: off-CPU redo flush time of connection threads
signals.condition: material share of foreground time
signals.why: This is the time a write cache could shrink.

impact_bound: At most the redo-flush + doublewrite/data-write wait share of foreground time, times (1 - cached_latency/uncached_latency). Typical: high (several-fold commit throughput) on consumer SSD/HDD with cache off; none with PLP drives. DURABILITY risk without power-loss protection.

experiment.change: enable volatile write cache (only acceptable when durability trade-off is accepted or PLP present)
experiment.predict: w_await falls sharply; redo fsync latency falls; commit-bound throughput rises
experiment.confirm_or_refute: Large fall in w_await confirms; no change means cache absent or already effective.
experiment.cost_or_risk: Data loss/corruption on power failure without PLP (kernel still issues flushes, but drive may lie).

collected: partly - disk await and off-CPU redo flush collected; add write_cache state (sysfs) and per-device flush latency

relevant_to: os; InnoDB with innodb_use_native_aio=ON (MySQL/PS use libaio; MariaDB 10.6+ may use io_uring, which is not limited by aio-max-nr). Cannot matter if io_setup succeeds at startup.

signals.metric: /proc/sys/fs/aio-nr vs /proc/sys/fs/aio-max-nr
signals.condition: aio-nr close to aio-max-nr (several mysqld instances or many io threads)
signals.why: io_setup() fails with EAGAIN when the system-wide limit is reached.

signals.metric: mysqld error log: 'io_setup() failed with EAGAIN' / native AIO disabled; SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES innodb_use_native_aio
signals.condition: message present or native AIO turned off at startup
signals.why: InnoDB falls back to simulated AIO (or fails to start), reducing I/O concurrency.

impact_bound: Binary: none if io_setup succeeded; if native AIO was lost, up to the share of time in data page read/flush waits that parallel I/O would overlap. Typical: none for single-instance hosts (default 65536 suffices).

experiment.predict: error log message disappears; innodb_use_native_aio effective; read/flush wait falls
experiment.confirm_or_refute: If no EAGAIN message existed, the change cannot matter - skip.
experiment.cost_or_risk: None (kernel memory only when used).

collected: no - add /proc/sys/fs/aio-nr and an error-log grep for io_setup

relevant_to: os; MySQL/PS/MariaDB with large_pages=ON (pairs with that variable); no effect when large_pages=OFF; MySQL 8.4+ falls back to normal pages if reservation is insufficient.

signals.metric: /proc/meminfo HugePages_Total/HugePages_Free/HugePages_Rsvd after startup
signals.condition: large_pages=ON but HugePages_Free ~= Total (buffer pool not using them) or error log 'Warning: Failed to allocate ... huge pages'
signals.why: Reservation too small: the buffer pool silently uses 4K pages.

signals.metric: perf: dTLB-load-misses / dTLB-loads and page-walk cycles (dtlb_load_misses.walk_active) of mysqld
signals.condition: a material share of mysqld cycles spent in page walks on a large buffer pool
signals.why: Huge pages cut TLB misses for buffer-pool access.

signals.metric: /proc/meminfo MemAvailable after reservation
signals.condition: reserved but unused huge pages, or memory pressure caused by the reservation
signals.why: Reserved huge pages are unavailable for anything else.

impact_bound: At most the share of mysqld CPU cycles spent in page walks (typically 2-10% on CPU-bound large-pool workloads). Typical: low to medium; none on I/O-bound runs.

experiment.change: reserve ceil(buffer_pool_size*1.05/2MiB) pages and set large_pages=ON
experiment.predict: page-walk cycles and dTLB misses fall; mysqld CPU ms per trx falls
experiment.confirm_or_refute: Confirm via walk cycles drop plus CPU/trx drop; refute if CPU/trx unchanged.
experiment.cost_or_risk: Memory locked away; pool cannot grow beyond reservation; restart required.

collected: partly - CPU profile collected; add /proc/meminfo HugePages_* and perf dTLB/page-walk counters

relevant_to: os; multi-socket or multi-NUMA-node hosts only (numactl -H shows >1 node); no effect on single-node VMs.

signals.metric: /proc/vmstat numa_hint_faults, numa_pages_migrated, numa_pte_updates rates
signals.condition: high hint-fault/migration rates during steady state
signals.why: Balancing unmaps pages to sample access, adding minor faults and migrations; for a shared buffer pool accessed from all nodes migrations do not help.

signals.metric: perf: share of mysqld CPU in task_numa_work/do_numa_page/migrate_pages
signals.condition: a material share of CPU
signals.why: Direct CPU cost of the balancing mechanism.

signals.metric: /proc/vmstat numa_hit/numa_miss/numa_foreign, perf remote-DRAM loads
signals.condition: high remote access share with stable thread placement
signals.why: Balancing could co-locate memory with threads.

impact_bound: At most the CPU share in NUMA hinting faults/migration plus minor-fault stalls. Typical: low (0-5%) for mysqld; none on single-node hosts.

experiment.predict: numa_hint_faults and numa_pages_migrated go to ~0; mysqld sys CPU and minor faults fall
experiment.confirm_or_refute: Gain with fallen sys CPU confirms; if remote memory access rises and CPU/trx rises, refute.
experiment.cost_or_risk: Loss of locality for workloads with node-local thread groups.

collected: no - add /proc/vmstat numa_* and node count

relevant_to: os; only when other process groups (sessions) compete for CPU on the host, e.g. the benchmark client or backups in another session; no effect for services under systemd (each is already in its own cgroup) unless CPU is saturated.

signals.metric: per-thread run-queue wait of mysqld threads and PSI cpu some
signals.condition: material run-queue wait while another session-group runs CPU-heavy work
signals.why: Autogroup gives each session group equal share, so mysqld's many threads may get the same CPU as a single client process.

signals.metric: /proc/<pid>/autogroup of mysqld and of competing processes
signals.condition: mysqld and competitors in different autogroups with CPU saturated
signals.why: Confirms the fairness mechanism is active.

impact_bound: Bounded by mysqld run-queue wait share under CPU saturation. Typical: none to low.

experiment.predict: mysqld run-queue wait falls when CPU is saturated
experiment.confirm_or_refute: No saturation means no possible effect; refute if run-queue wait unchanged.
experiment.cost_or_risk: Competing interactive processes may get less CPU.

collected: partly - run-queue wait and PSI collected; add autogroup membership

relevant_to: os; all flavors; matters with many concurrent threads, frequent per-query allocations (sorts, joins, tmp tables) or memory growth/fragmentation. Percona Server and MariaDB packages often ship jemalloc; MySQL uses glibc by default.

signals.metric: perf CPU profile share in malloc/free/arena locks (_int_malloc, malloc_consolidate, __lll_lock_wait in arena, je_*/tc_* functions)
signals.condition: a material share of mysqld CPU in allocator functions
signals.why: A scalable allocator (jemalloc/tcmalloc) reduces lock contention and per-call cost.

signals.metric: off-CPU futex waits with allocator frames in the stack
signals.condition: material share
signals.why: Arena lock contention in glibc.

signals.metric: mysqld RSS vs sum of configured buffers and performance_schema.memory_summary_global_by_event_name total; RSS growth over time
signals.condition: RSS materially above tracked memory, or growing steadily
signals.why: Fragmentation / unreturned memory in glibc arenas (MALLOC_ARENA_MAX or jemalloc fixes).

impact_bound: At most the allocator CPU + allocator-lock off-CPU share of foreground time; memory saving bounded by RSS - tracked memory. Typical: medium (5-20%) at high concurrency with glibc; low otherwise.

experiment.change: LD_PRELOAD jemalloc (or tcmalloc) or set glibc MALLOC_ARENA_MAX, restart
experiment.predict: allocator CPU share falls; mysqld CPU ms per trx falls; RSS lower/stable
experiment.confirm_or_refute: Confirm with profile shift; if allocator share was <2% any throughput change is noise.
experiment.cost_or_risk: Restart; allocator-specific memory overhead; rare bugs with some versions.

collected: partly - CPU profile collected (ensure an 'allocator' category); add RSS vs performance_schema memory_summary totals

relevant_to: os; ext4 (and remounts) on drives with a volatile write cache; no effect on drives with PLP or write_cache='write through' (kernel skips flushes) and on xfs (option removed).

signals.metric: /sys/block/<dev>/queue/write_cache and flush latency (eBPF block rq for REQ_PREFLUSH/FUA)
signals.condition: volatile cache present and cache flushes take a material share of fsync time
signals.why: Barriers issue cache flushes on every journal commit/fsync.

signals.metric: off-CPU redo flush time of connection threads
signals.condition: material share of foreground time
signals.why: Upper bound of what removing flushes can save.

impact_bound: At most the cache-flush portion of fsync time times fsyncs on the critical path. Typical: medium-high on consumer SSD/HDD; none with PLP. DURABILITY risk.

experiment.change: mount -o remount,nobarrier (only with accepted durability trade-off)
experiment.predict: fsync latency falls; commit-bound throughput rises
experiment.confirm_or_refute: No fall in fsync latency means flushes were not the cost (PLP) - revert.
experiment.cost_or_risk: Filesystem/database corruption on power loss.

collected: partly - fsyncs and off-CPU redo flush collected; add device flush-request latency

relevant_to: os; filesystems mounted with atime/strictatime; with the common default relatime, access-time updates happen at most once a day per file, so practically no effect for InnoDB (few long-open files).

signals.metric: mount options of datadir (/proc/mounts)
signals.condition: 'strictatime' or 'atime' present
signals.why: Every read updates inode atime, generating metadata writes.

signals.metric: journal/metadata writes (jbd2 commits) during read-only runs
signals.condition: write I/O during a read-only workload not explained by MySQL
signals.why: atime updates show up as metadata writes.

impact_bound: At most the metadata write I/O share; with relatime ~none. Typical: none to low.

experiment.predict: metadata write IOPS during read-only load fall
experiment.confirm_or_refute: No write change: refute.
experiment.cost_or_risk: Tools relying on atime break (rare).

collected: no - add datadir mount options

relevant_to: os; multi-NUMA-node hosts only. Related DB vars: innodb_numa_interleave (MySQL/PS 8.0+). No effect on single-node hosts.

signals.metric: numastat -p mysqld (per-node memory of mysqld)
signals.condition: buffer pool memory heavily skewed to one node while threads run on all nodes, or one node exhausted while others free
signals.why: Imbalanced allocation causes remote access and local-node reclaim/swap of mysqld memory.

signals.metric: /proc/vmstat numa_miss, numa_foreign, plus pswpout/pgscan on one node (/sys/devices/system/node/node*/vmstat)
signals.condition: swapping or reclaim on one node while other nodes have free memory
signals.why: Classic 'swap insanity': interleave spreads the pool.

signals.metric: perf remote vs local DRAM loads (mem_load_l3_miss_retired.remote_dram)
signals.condition: remote share high
signals.why: Bind to one node can help if mysqld fits on one node.

impact_bound: Bounded by the reclaim/swap stall time on the full node plus the remote-access latency share of memory stalls. Typical: low for steady performance, high for avoiding swap on multi-socket hosts with large buffer pools.

experiment.change: set NUMAPolicy=interleave (or bind to one node if mysqld fits), restart
experiment.predict: numastat per-node balance changes as intended; per-node swap/reclaim stops; CPU/trx flat or lower
experiment.confirm_or_refute: Confirm by stalls/swap disappearing; if only throughput noise moves, keep default.
experiment.cost_or_risk: Restart; bind can starve mysqld of memory/CPUs of other nodes.

collected: no - add numastat per node and node vmstat

relevant_to: os; only affects egress queues of NICs created after change (or reattached); matters for networks with loss/queuing and bulk replies (large result sets, replication over WAN). Matters only when clients connect over TCP from another host (or loopback at very high rates); no effect on Unix-socket clients.

signals.metric: tc -s qdisc show: drops, overlimits, backlog
signals.condition: drops or standing backlog on the egress qdisc
signals.why: Queueing discipline determines egress queueing delay and drops.

signals.metric: nstat TcpRetransSegs, TcpExtTCPLostRetransmit; ss -ti rtt/cwnd
signals.condition: retransmissions or RTT inflation under load
signals.why: fq (with pacing) reduces bursts and bufferbloat, and is required for older BBR.

impact_bound: At most the share of client time spent waiting on network transfer beyond base RTT. Typical: none on a LAN with small result sets; low-medium for bulk transfer over WAN.

experiment.change: set default_qdisc=fq (re-apply qdisc on the NIC)
experiment.predict: egress drops/backlog and retransmissions fall; response time for large results falls
experiment.confirm_or_refute: If qdisc stats show no drops/backlog before, refute up front.
experiment.cost_or_risk: Minimal; slightly higher CPU on very high packet rates.

collected: no - add tc qdisc stats and TCP retransmit counters (nstat)

relevant_to: os; high packet rates (many small queries per second over TCP) where NET_RX softirq runs out of budget. Matters only when clients connect over TCP from another host (or loopback at very high rates); no effect on Unix-socket clients.

signals.metric: /proc/net/softnet_stat column 3 (time_squeeze) per CPU
signals.condition: time_squeeze increasing during the run
signals.why: Softirq stopped with packets still pending because budget or time ran out.

signals.metric: %soft per CPU and ksoftirqd CPU
signals.condition: softirq time starving mysqld threads on the same CPU
signals.why: A larger budget lets softirq run longer, delaying user threads.

impact_bound: Bounded by the latency of packets deferred to ksoftirqd; typical: none to low (default 300 is enough below ~1M pps).

experiment.predict: time_squeeze rate falls; network latency/throughput under high pps improves
experiment.confirm_or_refute: No time_squeeze before means no possible effect.
experiment.cost_or_risk: Longer softirq bursts can increase latency for co-located threads.

collected: no - add /proc/net/softnet_stat (processed, dropped, time_squeeze) per CPU

relevant_to: os; same as netdev_budget (the time limit of a softirq round, default 2000 us). Matters only when clients connect over TCP from another host (or loopback at very high rates); no effect on Unix-socket clients.

signals.metric: /proc/net/softnet_stat time_squeeze
signals.condition: time_squeeze increasing while packet count per round is below netdev_budget
signals.why: The time budget, not the packet budget, ended the round.

impact_bound: As netdev_budget; typical none to low.

experiment.predict: time_squeeze falls
experiment.confirm_or_refute: No time_squeeze: no effect possible.
experiment.cost_or_risk: Longer softirq occupancy of a CPU.

collected: no - add softnet_stat

relevant_to: os; packet bursts on one CPU (RPS or non-NAPI paths) exceeding the per-CPU backlog. Matters only when clients connect over TCP from another host (or loopback at very high rates); no effect on Unix-socket clients.

signals.metric: /proc/net/softnet_stat column 2 (dropped) per CPU
signals.condition: dropped increasing during the run
signals.why: Packets dropped when the per-CPU input backlog is full cause TCP retransmits.

signals.metric: nstat TcpRetransSegs
signals.condition: retransmissions coinciding with softnet drops
signals.why: Drops turn into retransmission timeouts (200 ms+) for clients.

impact_bound: At most the retransmission delay share of client time; zero when softnet drops are zero. Typical: none; high in rare cases (RTO stalls).

experiment.predict: softnet dropped -> 0, retransmits fall, tail latency falls
experiment.confirm_or_refute: No drops before: skip.
experiment.cost_or_risk: Slightly more memory, potentially more queueing latency.

collected: no - add softnet_stat dropped and TCP retransmits

relevant_to: os; caps SO_RCVBUF set explicitly by applications (MySQL does not set it; autotuning uses tcp_rmem[2] instead). Effect only for applications calling setsockopt; for mysqld practically none. Matters only when clients connect over TCP from another host (or loopback at very high rates); no effect on Unix-socket clients.

signals.metric: ss -tmi: rcv_space / rb (skmem) of mysqld sockets vs bandwidth-delay product
signals.condition: an application sets SO_RCVBUF and receive window limits throughput on high-BDP links
signals.why: Explicit buffer sizes are clamped to rmem_max.

impact_bound: No measurable signal for mysqld under default settings; bounded by transfer time of large inserts/replication over high-BDP links. Typical: none.

experiment.predict: only matters if bulk-receive throughput was window-limited (ss shows rcv_wnd full)
experiment.confirm_or_refute: Unchanged ss rcv window: no effect.
experiment.cost_or_risk: Memory per socket if applications request large buffers.

relevant_to: os; only with RFS enabled (rps_flow_cnt>0 on RX queues and RPS on); otherwise no effect. Matters only when clients connect over TCP from another host (or loopback at very high rates); no effect on Unix-socket clients.

signals.metric: per-CPU %soft vs CPU where the consuming mysqld thread runs (cache misses in tcp_v4_rcv)
signals.condition: RPS on, many flows, softirq processing on CPUs different from the consuming thread
signals.why: RFS steers packets to the CPU running the consuming thread for cache locality; table too small causes collisions.

impact_bound: No direct counter; bounded by softirq + network-stack CPU share. Kernel doc suggests 32768-65536 for moderately loaded servers. Typical: none to low.

experiment.change: set rps_sock_flow_entries=32768 and rps_flow_cnt per queue = entries/queues
experiment.predict: network-stack CPU per trx falls; latency falls slightly
experiment.confirm_or_refute: Compare network-category CPU per trx in profile.
experiment.cost_or_risk: Little memory.

collected: partly - network CPU category collected; add RPS/RFS config state

relevant_to: os; caps MySQL back_log (listen backlog). Matters only with connection storms (many new connections per second, e.g. no pooling); MySQL default back_log = max_connections-based, capped by somaxconn (default 4096 on kernels >=5.4).

signals.condition: increasing during the run
signals.why: Accept queue full: SYNs/ACKs dropped, clients retry after 1s+ (SYN retransmit).

signals.condition: Recv-Q reaches Send-Q (backlog)
signals.why: Accept queue saturation.

signals.metric: Connections rate and Aborted_connects
signals.condition: high connect rate with client-side connect timeouts
signals.why: Corroborates connection storm.

impact_bound: At most the connect-retry delay times the number of overflowed connects; zero without overflows. Typical: none with pooled connections; high for connection-storm workloads.

experiment.predict: ListenOverflows -> 0; connect latency p99 falls
experiment.confirm_or_refute: No overflows before: no effect possible.
experiment.cost_or_risk: None significant.

relevant_to: os; caps SO_SNDBUF set explicitly by applications; mysqld does not set it, autotuning uses tcp_wmem[2]. Practically no effect for mysqld. Matters only when clients connect over TCP from another host (or loopback at very high rates); no effect on Unix-socket clients.

signals.metric: ss -tmi snd buffer (tb) and 'sndbuf_limited' time (ss -i shows sndbuf_limited)
signals.condition: a process sets SO_SNDBUF and sends are sndbuf-limited on high-BDP links

experiment.predict: sndbuf_limited time falls (only if explicit SO_SNDBUF)
experiment.confirm_or_refute: No sndbuf_limited: no effect.
